ai.title: Relax assistant message pause limit 3 to 6
ai.summary: mainPrompt increases shouldPause threshold from 3 to 6 consecutive assistant messages in backend/src/main-prompt.ts. getExtraInstructionForUserPrompt now accepts justUsedATool and numAssistantMessages, gating plan_complex_change suggestions on tool usage. conversation-progress.ts adds example phrase for unbounded iteration detection. Scope limited to backend conversation logic.

eli5.text: The assistant that works behind the scenes on coding tasks will now keep going for up to six rounds in a row before stopping to check in with you, instead of stopping after only three. This means it can make more consecutive suggestions or fixes without pausing for your input each time. The same spot in the system now also mentions a new example of when you've asked it to run continuously until something is done, and a helper that decides what guidance to give now takes in whether you just used a tool and how many times the assistant has spoken. The change is live today and only affects the part of the system that manages the back-and-forth conversation between you and the assistant.

ai.title: Swap tiktoken for gpt-tokenizer in backend
ai.summary: Replaces `tiktoken` with `gpt-tokenizer` 2.8.1 for token counting in `backend/src/util/token-counter.ts`. Imports `encode` from `gpt-tokenizer/esm/model/gpt-4o` instead of instantiating an `encoding_for_model` encoder, simplifying the count logic to a direct function call. Scope is limited to the backend dependency list and token utility. The fallback behavior remains `Math.ceil(text.length / 3)` on error.

eli5.text: The system that counts how much text fits into a request was rebuilt behind the scenes. Previously it used one library to measure tokens, and now it uses a different one, though the result it produces is the same. If you looked, you wouldn't see any visible difference; nothing about how the system operates changed today.

ai.title: Force unbounded iteration for plan execution
ai.summary: backend/src/main-prompt.ts now detects if the assistant is executing a plan by checking for 'plan_complex_change' in the response. If detected, allowUnboundedIterationPromise resolves true immediately, bypassing the checkToAllowUnboundedIteration call. The logic for handling generated plans was refactored to trigger a 'continue' tool call with a specific implementation prompt instead of manually setting state flags. System instruction tags in getExtraInstructionForUserPrompt were renamed from <important_instruction> to <system_instruction>.

eli5.text: The assistant now notices when it is in the middle of carrying out a multi-step plan (a sequence it generated to solve a task) and, at that moment, removes the usual cap on how many steps it can take before pausing for your input. Instead of relying on an external permission check each time, it continues on its own until the plan is fully implemented, which is what you would see if you walked away for a few minutes and returned to a completed change rather than a half-finished draft. The internal labels the assistant uses to organize its instructions were also renamed, but that has no visible effect on you.

ai.title: Expand planning file selection prompt
ai.summary: Refined the user prompt in `getRelevantFilesForPlanning` within `backend/src/planning.ts`. The instruction now explicitly requests `knowledge.md`, example code, tests, and second-order files to improve context gathering. This change targets the internal planning subsystem to ensure more comprehensive file retrieval for complex requests.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to plan a coding task, it now searches your project for more types of files, including documentation, example code, tests, and related files, so it can gather better context before starting. You won't see this directly, but the assistant's internal planning step will now pull in more relevant files, leading to more complete and accurate plans for complex requests. This change is live today and only affects the internal planning process, not your direct interaction.

ai.title: Add terminal command check instruction to main prompt
ai.summary: Added conditional instruction in `getExtraInstructionForUserPrompt` requiring agents to run specified terminal commands (e.g., type/test checks) after changes if defined in knowledge files. This ensures automated validation steps embedded in project knowledge are executed. Scope limited to `backend/src/main-prompt.ts`.

eli5.text: When the assistant finishes helping you, it now checks your project's own notes to see if there are specific verification commands it should run (like checking for errors) at the end of the response. This only happens if your project documentation actually lists those commands, and it ensures the automated checks your team set up are actually executed after changes are made.

ai.title: Conditional minimal-edit instruction in agent mode
ai.summary: System prompt logic in backend/src/main-prompt.ts now conditionally omits the 'minimal edits' and 'pause for instructions' directive when allowUnboundedIteration is true. This allows the agent to perform more extensive changes without stopping for user input during unbounded iterations. The change propagates the allowUnboundedIteration flag through getExtraInstructionForUserPrompt.

eli5.text: When the assistant runs in a fully automated mode, it no longer tells itself to make only small, tentative edits and then stop for your approval. Instead, it can keep making changes as needed until the task is complete. This only affects situations where the software is set to run without pausing for your input between steps, letting it work through a job end-to-end without stopping. You'd only notice if you're running that kind of hands-off automation, where the assistant now goes ahead and makes whatever edits are necessary rather than holding back.
